GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) gets **about 45% accuracy** when the key is at the 200th position of 300. This is the lowest point on its curve. It is an estimate read off a plot: the paper gives no exact figure for it.

- **Where it comes from:** Figure 7, right panel, "300 Key-Value Pairs (~16K tokens)" (p. 7). The gpt-3.5-turbo-16k-0613 line starts near 100% at the 1st position. It is about 95% at the 100th position, about 70% at the 150th, and drops to about 45% at the 200th. It then rises to about 73% at the 250th position and back to about 100% at the 300th.
- **Why it's only an estimate:** The text layer of p. 7 has only the axis labels for this figure. The appendix has full results tables for multi-document QA (pp. 18–19), but the key-value task's appendix table only counts tokens (Table 4, p. 17). So I read the value from the rendered page.
- **Context:** The paper says that GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) and MPT-30B-Instruct do worst when the key-value pair is in the middle of the context (p. 6). In the same panel, Claude-1.3 and Claude-1.3 (100K) stay near 100% (pp. 6–7).

The same model gets near-perfect accuracy on this setting with query-aware contextualization (the query placed both before and after the data), but that is a different experiment (p. 8).
